OPEN’IX AI
Complete Production-Ready Platform Blueprint & Master Development Prompt
Open’Ix Intelligence OS
AI Chat • Model Hub • Prompt Studio • Knowledge • AI Agents • Workflows
A complete original product specification for planning, designing, building, testing, securing, deploying, and
operating an AI-powered workspace platform.
Design Principle: Build an original Open’Ix product identity and implementation. Reference screenshots may inspire useful
product patterns, but no proprietary branding, logos, or exact layouts should be copied.
Open’Ix AI — Production Blueprint Page 1
1. Executive Product Vision
Open’Ix AI Intelligence OS is a unified AI workspace where users can talk with AI models, manage reusable
prompts, create agents, organize knowledge, experiment with AI, and automate workflows from one connected
platform.
The platform is designed around a shared intelligence layer: authorized workspace and project knowledge can
provide relevant context to AI features without requiring users to repeat important instructions.
Core product flow: User → Workspace → Project → Knowledge & Context → AI Model/Agent → Tools &
Workflows → Results → History & Learning
Production-ready means the system should have clear requirements, validation, testing, observability,
security controls, deployment processes, and rollback plans. No software can honestly promise zero bugs;
the goal is robust engineering and systematic quality assurance.

AI Chat Multi-model conversations with files, authorized knowledge context, conversation history, Model Hub Search, compare, select, configure, and route supported AI providers and models.
Prompt Studio My Prompts Knowledge Hub AI Agents AI Lab Workflows Visual or structured automation using triggers, AI steps, tools, conditions, approvals, and 3. Knowledge Hub — Intelligence Foundation
Project Knowledge belongs to a specific project and can contain purpose, goals, target users, architecture,
APIs, database information, business rules, coding standards, documents, and project-specific AI instructions.
Workspace Knowledge contains reusable rules shared across authorized projects: brand guidelines,
development standards, preferred stack, naming conventions, design principles, language and tone, security
policies, and organizational instructions.
Knowledge pipeline: Source → Validation → Processing → Organization → Permission Check → Retrieval →
Context Assembly → AI Response/Action → Audit
• Manual notes and structured instructions
• Document and file ingestion with source metadata
• Approved website or cloud reference connectors
• Collections, tags, search, source freshness, and version history
• Explicit scope: workspace, project, team, or private
Open’Ix AI — Production Blueprint Page 2
• Role-based permissions and audit records
• Context previews so users can understand what information was used
• Retention and deletion controls for workspace data
4. Workspace and Project Context Rules
The context system should not blindly inject every document into every AI request. It should resolve the active
workspace and project, check permissions, retrieve only relevant material, respect token/context limits, and make
the source scope auditable.
Recommended precedence: Security & platform policy → Organization/workspace rules → Project rules →
Agent configuration → User request. More specific instructions may refine general instructions but must not
bypass higher-priority safety or security controls.
5. AI Chat Experience
• New conversation, rename, archive, search, and history management
• Model selector with provider capabilities and availability states
• Response length, creativity, tone, and tool-use controls
• File attachments and authorized knowledge context
• Streaming responses, cancellation, retry, copy, feedback, and citations where applicable
• Clear loading, empty, error, offline, and rate-limit states
• Desktop, tablet, and mobile responsive layouts
6. AI Agents
An AI Agent is a configurable software assistant that can pursue a user-approved goal through a controlled loop
of understanding, planning, using authorized knowledge and tools, checking results, and returning an outcome.
Agent execution flow: Goal → Context Resolution → Plan → Permission/Policy Check → Tool Execution →
Observation → Next Step → Validation → Result & Log
• Agent identity, purpose, instructions, and personality/tone
• Approved tools and integrations with least-privilege permissions
• Knowledge collections and project/workspace scope
• Memory settings with user-visible controls
• Budgets, timeouts, retries, rate limits, and execution limits
• Human approval gates for consequential external actions
• Run history, logs, outputs, and error reporting
7. Design System
Identity: Premium, calm, futuristic AI workspace. Original Open’Ix visual language with deep charcoal and
midnight surfaces, sophisticated purple and electric-violet accents, soft white typography, subtle borders, and
Open’Ix AI — Production Blueprint Page 3
restrained glass effects.
• Do not reproduce another product's exact layout, logo, illustrations, or distinctive visual identity.
• Use a reusable token system for colors, spacing, typography, radii, shadows, and motion.
• Maintain WCAG-oriented contrast and keyboard-accessible interaction patterns.
• Use responsive breakpoints and touch-friendly controls.
• Provide dark mode first, with a coherent light mode if supported.
8. Recommended Production Architecture
Frontend: Next.js + TypeScript + React + accessible component system + Tailwind CSS or equivalent
token-driven styling.
Backend: A modular API service such as NestJS or FastAPI, with explicit domain boundaries and background
workers for long-running jobs.
Data: PostgreSQL for relational data; Redis for caching/queues where appropriate; object storage for files; a
vector/search system selected according to retrieval requirements.
AI Layer: Provider abstraction, model registry, routing, streaming gateway, tool execution boundary, evaluation,
usage tracking, and graceful provider fallback where product policy permits.
Infrastructure: Containerized services, managed secrets, CI/CD, environment separation, monitoring, backups,
and documented rollback procedures.
9. Core Data Domains
• Identity: users, organizations, workspaces, memberships, roles
• Projects: projects, environments, settings, collaborators
• Knowledge: sources, documents, chunks/indexes, collections, versions, permissions
• AI: providers, models, capabilities, routing policies, usage records
• Chat: conversations, messages, attachments, citations, feedback
• Prompts: prompts, versions, tags, folders, templates, shares
• Agents: definitions, tools, runs, checkpoints, memory policies, approvals
• Workflows: definitions, versions, triggers, runs, steps, logs
• Operations: audit events, notifications, billing/entitlements, support signals
10. API and Service Principles
• Version public APIs and validate all input at trust boundaries.
• Use authentication and authorization checks on every protected resource.
• Prefer idempotency for external actions and background jobs.
• Return structured errors without exposing secrets or internal implementation details.
• Use pagination, filtering, and rate limiting for scalable APIs.
Open’Ix AI — Production Blueprint Page 4
• Document contracts using OpenAPI or equivalent.
11. Security and Privacy Baseline
• Secure authentication, session management, and optional MFA according to product requirements
• Role- and resource-based authorization with tenant/workspace isolation
• Encryption in transit and appropriate encryption at rest
• Secrets stored in a dedicated secret-management system, never hard-coded
• File validation, malware scanning where applicable, and safe content handling
• Audit logs for sensitive administrative and knowledge-access actions
• Dependency scanning, security review, and incident response procedures
• Data export, deletion, and retention controls appropriate to the jurisdictions served
12. Quality Assurance and Testing
• Unit tests for domain logic and critical utilities
• Integration tests for APIs, authorization, database behavior, and provider adapters
• End-to-end tests for primary user journeys
• Accessibility testing and keyboard navigation checks
• Responsive testing across supported viewport categories
• Performance budgets and load testing for critical services
• Failure tests for provider outages, queue failures, invalid files, and partial workflow execution
• Pre-release staging validation and production smoke checks
13. Deployment and Operations
Environment path: Local Development → Automated CI → Preview/Staging → Production
• Separate development, staging, and production configuration
• Automated linting, type checking, tests, and security checks before release
• Database migrations with backups and rollback strategy
• Health checks, structured logs, metrics, tracing, and alerting
• Feature flags for controlled rollout
• Release notes and version tracking
• Incident procedures and documented recovery runbooks
14. Definition of Done
• Feature requirements and acceptance criteria are implemented
• Authorization and validation are reviewed
Open’Ix AI — Production Blueprint Page 5
• Tests cover critical behavior
• Loading, empty, error, and edge states are handled
• Responsive and accessibility checks are completed
• Telemetry and meaningful error logging are present
• Documentation and environment configuration are updated
• Deployment has been tested in a staging-like environment
• Rollback or mitigation approach is documented for meaningful changes
15. Complete Master Build Prompt
You are the product, design, engineering, and quality intelligence layer for Open’Ix AI Intelligence OS. Build
an original, production-oriented AI workspace platform that connects AI Chat, Model Hub, Prompt Studio, My
Prompts, Knowledge Hub, AI Agents, AI Lab, and Workflows. Use Workspace Knowledge as shared context
for authorized projects and Project Knowledge for project-specific context. Never treat knowledge as globally
accessible by default. Resolve scope and permissions before retrieval, retrieve only relevant sources, and
provide auditable context handling. Create a scalable architecture with clear modules, typed contracts,
secure APIs, background processing for long-running jobs, reliable file handling, observability, testing, and
deployment procedures. Prefer maintainable, accessible, responsive components and a consistent
design-token system. Use an original Open’Ix identity: deep charcoal and midnight surfaces with refined
deep-purple and electric-violet accents, soft white typography, subtle borders, and calm futuristic
interactions. Do not copy another company’s branding, logo, proprietary assets, or exact interface layouts.
For every feature: understand the goal, identify requirements and edge cases, design the user flow, define
data and permissions, implement reusable components and services, validate input, handle failures
gracefully, test critical paths, document assumptions, and prepare deployment safely. For AI Agents, use
controlled execution with approved tools, least privilege, budgets, timeouts, run logs, and human approval
gates when external or consequential actions require confirmation. Do not claim software is bug-free.
Instead, use automated testing, reviews, monitoring, staging validation, and rollback readiness to reduce
defects and operate reliably. Deliver implementation-ready specifications, code structures, test plans, and
deployment checklists that a professional engineering team can execute.
16. Suggested Build Roadmap
Phase 1 — Foundation — Identity, workspace/project model, design system, authentication, authorization,
database foundation.
Phase 2 — Core Intelligence — AI Chat, provider abstraction, model registry, conversation history, usage
controls.
Phase 3 — Knowledge — Workspace/Project Knowledge, ingestion, retrieval, permissions, auditability.
Phase 4 — Creation — Prompt Studio, prompt library, templates, versions, testing.
Phase 5 — Agents — Agent builder, tools, knowledge access, runs, approvals, logs.
Phase 6 — Automation — Workflow definitions, triggers, workers, execution history.
Phase 7 — Quality & Operations — Security hardening, evaluations, analytics, monitoring, CI/CD, production
readiness.
Open’Ix AI — Production Blueprint Page 6
Final Product Direction
Open’Ix AI should feel like a connected intelligence workspace rather than a collection of disconnected AI tools.
Knowledge provides context, models provide intelligence, prompts provide reusable intent, agents perform
structured tasks, and workflows connect repeatable processes.
This blueprint is a complete foundation for professional product planning and implementation. Individual
provider APIs, hosting choices, legal/privacy requirements, pricing, and deployment credentials should be
selected and configured during implementation according to the target market and operational needs.
